subject: Post-call recap: embeddings fit & next steps for Semanticscope
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Howard <alex@semanticscope.com>; Sally Chang <sallyc@semanticscope.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: embeddings fit & next steps for Semanticscope

Hi Alex / Sally —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the experiments we discussed so we’re all aligned on next steps: 

1) Primary goal: improve Semanticscope search recall for product-help articles and cross-doc concept matching. Current system uses sentence-BERT embeddings (384d) and you’re seeing drift on new content categories (release notes, API changelogs).

2) Hypotheses we want to validate in a short POC (2–3 weeks):
- Switching to a 768d encoder (open-encoder-768) will reduce false negatives on short queries.
- Dimensionality + L2 normalization improvements will change nearest-neighbor ranking; test both cosine and inner-product.
- Prompt-set evaluation: include 40 warm-start queries and a 150-item human-labeled relevance set (will share).

3) Proposed experiments we’ll run on Redwood Dedicated POC nodes:
- Baseline: your current SBERT pipeline (embedding export + FAISS HNSW)
- Variant A: open-encoder-768, float16, L2 norm + cosine
- Variant B: open-encoder-768 quantized (8-bit) with fallback to full precision for top-25 rerank

4) Success metrics: semantic nDCG@10, MRR, and 95th percentile recall for queries that previously returned zero results. Target: +6–10 nDCG lift and reduce zero-hit queries by 50% on the labeled set.

5) Deliverables from Redwood by EOD Thu: short benchmark CSV, initial prompt-set (v1), and a 6-min demo screen recording of the run.

Please reply with any corrections on the hypotheses or to add anything I missed. If you’re good with this plan we’ll schedule the POC run next Tue/Wed and lock in test data access (S3 share or secure upload).

Thanks —
Rishi
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: embeddings-benchmark-summary.csv (stub), prompt-set-v1.txt (stub), demo-screen-recording.mp4 (link stub)

From: Alex Howard <alex@semanticscope.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: embeddings fit & next steps for Semanticscope

Rishi —

This is a great summary, thanks. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Data access: we prefer to give you an S3 read-only bucket with a manifest (will ping infra). ETA for the share: end of day Tuesday.
- Labeled set: we have 150 items but only ~60 are high-quality labels; we can prioritize those for the first run.
- Security: our Security com wants confirmation that the Dedicated POC nodes will not write logs to any shared Redwood buckets. Can your team confirm?

Also curious on how quantized Variant B impacts retrieval quality vs cost — if we can get a cost delta estimate that’d help our evaluation committee.

Thanks —
Alex
Head of Search, Semanticscope

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: embeddings fit & next steps for Semanticscope

Alex —

Quick answers to your security / quantization questions: 

- Dedicated POC isolation: confirmed. The Dedicated nodes for this engagement will be provisioned in a customer-isolated pool; no logs, artifacts, or model weights will be written to shared Redwood buckets unless you explicitly authorize. We’ll provide the POA and the network diagram in the onboarding doc.

- Quantization trade-offs: in our internal tests (open-encoder-768):
  • float16 baseline -> nDCG@10: 0.72 (cpu/gpu mix)
  • 8-bit quantized -> nDCG@10: 0.68 (drop ~0.04) but throughput/cost improves ~2.8x on inference; top-25 rerank with full precision recovers ~0.02 of that loss in many cases.

I’ve attached the benchmark CSV and the initial prompt set for your labeling team. Dev, can you schedule a 30-min run on Tue morning (9–11am PT) and share the Redwood run link?

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): embeddings-benchmark-summary.csv, prompt-set-v1.txt
